comment: Regression corpus for tools/bash_guard.py: [expect, command] pairs, run by --self-test against the template rules alone (an owner's local rules carry their own examples). Block cases are bypass attempts from adversarial reviews and real incidents; allow cases are everyday commands and past false alarms, kept so a fix cannot regress. A few cases go against the obvious reading by decision: a merge must pass the literal SHA it verified, not $(git rev-parse HEAD); rm -rf * after a cd must name its path; a bare env prints every exported key, so env | grep PATH blocks; a test runner given one shell variable stays local, since the guard cannot tell what it holds; and a deploy script run by hand is allowed, as a direct Wrangler deploy is. Payloads never run: the self-test only parses them (rules/gates.md). A case the guard cannot parse counts as an allow, as the hook reads it, so a block case must find a hit. Known limits: a program name held in a variable (S=security; $S ...); a case statement inside $(...); escaped backticks nested in backticks; a key variable named through another variable (${!n}, zsh's ${(P)n}); zsh flags outside double quotes (${(U)NAME}); a key read by an interpreter (os.environ, process.env) or expanded in a here-string, a heredoc body or another program's arguments; a GraphQL query read from a file (-F query=@q.graphql); --help anywhere skips every rule without past_help, so rm -rf ~ --help is allowed; and a copy of claude_os_sync.py run directly or by uv run shows the guard only its name, so a copy edited to skip its own source check gets through. Known false alarms: '$NAME' in single quotes blocks, since words reach the rules without their quotes; a multi-line string that holds a door command beside an unrelated process call blocks; and a doc edit whose perl program holds anything besides s///, tr/// and y/// statements is read whole. A session changes an org or repo ruleset and branch protection; deleting one still blocks.
